elements.quote: The Infectious Diseases Data Observatory (IDDO) has undertaken a living systematic review (LSR) to provide an open, accessible and frequently updated resource summarising characteristics of COVID-19 study registrations.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a (living) systematic review.

elements.quote: The Infectious Diseases Data Observatory (IDDO) has undertaken a living systematic review (LSR) to provide an open, accessible and frequently updated resource summarising characteristics of COVID-19 study registrations.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an explicit objective/review purpose.
The abstract does not specify main inclusion and exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: Methods: Review of all eligible trial records identified by systematic searches as of 3 April 2020 and initial synthesis of clinical study characteristics were conducted.
elements.reason: The abstract provides the time point for the search (as of 3 April 2020) but does not identify the information sources used.
The abstract does not describe methods used to assess risk of bias.

elements.quote: Methods: Review of all eligible trial records identified by systematic searches as of 3 April 2020 and initial synthesis of clinical study characteristics were conducted.
elements.reason: The abstract briefly states that an initial synthesis was conducted, but does not report detailed methods for presenting/synthesizing results.

elements.quote: Results: There were 728 study registrations which met eligibility criteria and were still active. Median (25 th , 75 th percentile) sample size was 130 (60, 400) for all studies and 134 (70, 300) for RCTs.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the total number of included studies (728) and summarizes study characteristics (e.g., median sample sizes), but it does not report the total number of participants.

elements.quote: Overall 109 pharmacological interventions or advanced therapy medicinal products covering 23 drug categories were studied. Majority (57%, 62/109) of them were planned only in one study arm, either alone or in combination with other interventions. There were 49 distinct combinations studied with 90% (44/49) of them administered in only one or two study arms.
elements.reason: The abstract provides numeric results describing the interventions/combinations, but it does not clearly present results for 'main outcomes' (e.g., outcome-specific effect estimates or outcome counts).

elements.quote: Methods: Review of all eligible trial records identified by systematic searches as of 3 April 2020 and initial synthesis of clinical study characteristics were conducted.
elements.reason: The abstract describes an initial synthesis of study characteristics and does not report a meta-analysis or summary estimate with a confidence/credible interval.

elements.quote: Results: There were 728 study registrations which met eligibility criteria and were still active.
elements.reason: The abstract reports characteristics and planned interventions of study registrations, not comparisons between groups; therefore no direction of effect/group favored is reported.

elements.quote: Conclusions: Baseline review highlighted that the majority of investigations in the first three months of the outbreak were small studies with unique treatment arms, likely to be unpowered to provide solid evidence.
elements.reason: The abstract summarizes an important limitation of the evidence (small/unpowered studies).

elements.quote: The continued work of this LSR will allow a more dependable overview of interventions tested, predict the likely strength of evidence generated, allow fast and informative filtering of relevant trials for specific user groups and provide the rapid guidance needed by investigators and funders to avoid duplication of efforts.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an overall interpretation and implications for use.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide a register name and registration number.

elements.quote: Conversely, independent trials with small sample sizes and underrepresentation of some patient populations limit the acquisition of substantive evidence to assess the effects and applicability of the many diagnostic methods, therapeutic and prophylactic strategies targeted to address the COVID-19 pandemic 3 .
elements.reason: The evidence describes limitations in the current evidence base (small trials, underrepresented populations) that imply important uncertainties, but it does not clearly detail the overall current state of knowledge and uncertainties in a comprehensive way.

elements.quote: The Infectious Diseases Data Observatory (IDDO) has undertaken a living systematic review (LSR) to provide an open, accessible and frequently updated resource summarising characteristics of COVID-19 study registrations.

No evidence is provided describing similar systematic reviews and explaining the need for the current review via updates/replications with citations to previous reviews.

This review concerns living systematic review of COVID-19 clinical trial registrations; no intervention effects or mechanism of action of an intervention is described in the retrieved evidence, so this conditional element does not apply.

No logic model for hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes is reported in the retrieved evidence; given the review is about summarising trial registration characteristics (not complex intervention evaluation), this conditional element does not apply.

elements.quote: This is a living systematic review of clinical study registrations (clinical trials and otherwise) for the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of COVID-19, an important endeavour in the midst of the pandemic and a concurrent infodemic with rapid evidence proliferation.

elements.quote: This is a living systematic review of clinical study registrations (clinical trials and otherwise) for the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of COVID-19, an important endeavour in the midst of the pandemic and a concurrent infodemic with rapid evidence proliferation.
elements.reason: The retrieved evidence describes a living systematic review of clinical study registrations, not a review of intervention effects with planned PICO-style comparisons; therefore the PICO comparison requirement is not applicable based on the provided text.

elements.quote: All clinical trial registrations either being planned, or currently underway to diagnose, treat or prevent COVID-19 were eligible for inclusion in the baseline results of this review. This included patients known to be infected with COVID-19 as well as healthy volunteers, healthcare workers or other patient populations where health related outcomes were assessed in the context of COVID-19. The review was not limited by outcome, language or intervention given the desire to capture all clinical trial registrations planning to or currently evaluating any COVID-19 diagnostic, prevention or treatment modality. Eligibility was not restricted to clinical trials only; no limitations on study design were applied so that all research and observational studies would be incorporated, including retrospective studies. All trial registry records included in the review are hereafter referred to as clinical 'study' registrations.
elements.reason: The eligibility basis for study question/participants (COVID-19 diagnosis/treatment/prevention and participant types), eligible study types/designs (no study design limitations), and lack of outcome language/intervention restrictions are specified. However, the evidence does not explicitly state all study-characteristic components such as follow-up requirements.

Full-text records screened and assessed for eligibility (n = 819)
Studies included in living systematic review (n = 790)
Studies included in baseline descriptive synthesis (n = 728)
Full-text articles excluded, with reasons (n = 29)
Cancelled Studies (n = 62)
elements.reason: The flow diagram reports records identified through search (leading to n=819 after duplicates), records screened (n=819), full-text excluded (n=29), cancelled (n=62), and studies included (n=790 living; n=728 baseline). However, it does not separately report the number removed before screening or the number excluded after initial screening with that terminology/stratification.

No explicit reporting is provided for the numbers of reports sought, not retrieved, assessed for eligibility, and excluded with primary reasons as separate counts (only some excluded/cancelled counts are shown).

elements.quote:
Studies included in living systematic review (n = 790)
Studies included in baseline descriptive synthesis (n = 728)
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the number of included studies for the living review and the baseline descriptive synthesis (n=790; n=728). It does not explicitly report the number of included reports (reports vs studies).

Although the review is a living systematic review, the provided evidence does not report ongoing studies and associated reports in the PRISMA study selection flow (i.e., as distinct selection counts).
The provided evidence does not report current selection results alongside the number of studies in the previous review.
The flow diagram and accompanying text do not distinguish records excluded by humans versus by automation tools.

elements.quote: Of the 819 unique records, 29 records were excluded because they did not include COVID-19 patients, and were not conducted in the context of COVID-19. Of the 790 records that met eligibility, 62 clinical trials were cancelled after registration and therefore excluded from further analysis.
elements.reason: The report provides exclusion reasons for subsets of records/trials (e.g., no COVID-19 patients/context; cancelled trials) but does not cite individual studies that might appear eligible and specify a reason for each excluded study.
No evidence is provided showing that each included study is individually cited.

elements.quote: As well as tabulating and graphing key characteristics of the registered COVID-19 clinical trials, the authors present engaging 'Cognitive City' visualizations of the registered trials by intervention. Conclusions drawn in the paper are supported by the results presented and the limitations and risks of bias are clearly addressed. Reviewer... Table 1: In this table the data are stratified by study design, but the current text formatting makes it difficult to discern the individual study design sections.
elements.reason: The evidence indicates that key characteristics are tabulated (e.g., Table 1 stratified by study design), but it does not demonstrate that the characteristics of every included study are presented in a table/figure that supports comparison across included studies.

Although the review concerns treatment interventions and mentions summary tables (e.g., Table 2), the evidence does not show an additional table summarising intervention details for every included study.

elements.quote: Accordingly, assessment of meta-biases or the strength of the body of evidence represented by included records are not relevant.
elements.reason: The retrieved evidence states that assessment of meta-bias/strength of evidence is not relevant, and it does not provide any tables/figures showing domain-level and overall risk-of-bias judgements for each included study.

elements.quote: Accordingly, assessment of meta-biases or the strength of the body of evidence represented by included records are not relevant.
elements.reason: No justifications for risk-of-bias judgements are presented in the retrieved evidence; instead, the text indicates such assessment is not relevant.

elements.quote: Accordingly, assessment of meta-biases or the strength of the body of evidence represented by included records are not relevant.
elements.reason: Outcome-specific risk-of-bias judgements alongside study results are not shown in the retrieved evidence.

The retrieved evidence describes how summary statistics were calculated (e.g., categorical proportions/frequencies; continuous totals/means/quartiles), but it does not report, for every outcome and every study, appropriate group-level summary statistics.

The retrieved evidence does not present effect estimates and their precision for outcomes by study; it only discusses descriptive statistics and figures about number of study arms/planned sample sizes.

Although figures are referenced/described (e.g., figures showing study arms and planned sample sizes), the retrieved evidence does not show that, whenever results are presented visually or in text, a tabular display is also provided.

elements.quote: No records were excluded at the title level, each record was reviewed in its entirety either as reported in WHO ICTRP or the source registry before assessment of eligibility.
elements.reason: This indicates that study-level data came from WHO ICTRP or from the source registry, but the retrieved evidence does not explicitly report the source of study-level data for each included study/outcome in the way required by the checklist item.

The retrieved evidence states that descriptive statistics were used to present extracted data, but it does not identify results that were computed/estimated rather than directly reported for outcomes by study.

elements.quote: In a first effort to distil the hierarchy of evidence being generated for COVID-19 interventions, registration details have been used to make a preliminary assessment of the strength and potential bias in relation to the design and intended execution within individual studies using the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine 2011 Levels of Evidence 22 .
elements.reason: The manuscript reports making a preliminary assessment of strength/potential bias within individual studies, but the retrieved evidence does not show that this is summarised for each synthesis (i.e., per synthesis characteristics and risk of bias among contributing studies).
The retrieved evidence does not identify the studies contributing to each synthesis.

elements.quote: Descriptive statistics were used to present the extracted data.
elements.reason: The evidence indicates that descriptive statistics (and summaries/figures) were used, but it does not explicitly confirm that all pre-specified and additional statistical syntheses were reported.
No meta-analysis summary estimates or their precision (e.g., confidence/credible intervals) are reported in the provided evidence.
No measures of statistical heterogeneity (e.g., I², τ²) for meta-analyses are reported in the provided evidence.
The provided evidence describes descriptive statistics and visualisation, but does not report synthesized results with precision for other statistical synthesis methods.
There is no reporting of synthesized results with relevant statistics for synthesis methods that do not produce effect estimates, in the provided evidence.
No comparisons of groups or directions of effect are reported in the provided evidence.
No mean-difference syntheses (or related details such as scale units/limits/MID) are reported in the provided evidence.
No re-expressed standardized mean difference syntheses (or instrument details) are reported in the provided evidence.
No results are reported describing investigations of possible causes of heterogeneity among study results (regardless of significance or direction).
No information is provided identifying studies contributing to each subgroup (no subgroup analysis results are evidenced).
No interpretation is reported that addresses the observational nature of heterogeneity analyses and possible confounding.
No subgroup analysis results are evidenced, including no interaction-test P values, subgroup estimates, precision, or heterogeneity.
No difference between subgroup effects and its precision is reported.
No meta-regression is evidenced; therefore coefficient P values and precision are not reported.
No meta-regression scatterplots are evidenced.
No results of informal heterogeneity investigations are described.
No sensitivity analyses are reported in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not discuss the robustness of the main analysis in light of any sensitivity analyses.
No tables comparing original results with sensitivity-analysis results/assumptions/contributing studies are reported in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not present sensitivity-analysis results in forest plots.

elements.quote: Accordingly, assessment of meta-biases or the strength of the body of evidence represented by included records are not relevant.
elements.reason: No risk-of-bias assessments due to missing results (arising from reporting biases) are presented for each synthesis assessed.

elements.reason: The document states that assessment of meta-biases/body-of-evidence strength is not relevant, and no risk-of-bias tool usage with item responses/judgements/supporting information is reported.

elements.quote: Accordingly, assessment of meta-biases or the strength of the body of evidence represented by included records are not relevant.
elements.reason: No funnel plot usage is reported; the evidence indicates that meta-bias assessment is not relevant for this living systematic review baseline.

elements.quote: Accordingly, assessment of meta-biases or the strength of the body of evidence represented by included records are not relevant.
elements.reason: No funnel-plot asymmetry test (and thus no exact P value/statistics) is reported.

elements.quote: Baseline results are limited to the initial data extraction, descriptive analysis of trial characteristics and visualisation of clinical trial registry records.
elements.reason: No sensitivity analyses examining missing results compared with a primary analysis are reported; the study describes baseline descriptive/visualization rather than synthesis-based sensitivity analyses.

elements.quote: Baseline results are limited to the initial data extraction, descriptive analysis of trial characteristics and visualisation of clinical trial registry records.
elements.reason: No selective non-reporting assessments in a study-by-synthesis matrix are reported.

elements.quote: Baseline results are limited to the initial data extraction, descriptive analysis of trial characteristics and visualisation of clinical trial registry records.
elements.reason: No studies with missing results displayed beneath forest plots or in a table are reported.
No overall certainty or confidence level for each important outcome is reported in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not explain reasons for rating certainty down or up.
There is no indication that certainty/confidence is communicated for outcomes using a section-appropriate format in the retrieved evidence.
No evidence summary tables (e.g., GRADE Summary of Findings) are reported in the retrieved evidence.

The retrieved evidence includes discussion of study findings and limitations (e.g., duplication, lack of coordination, and insufficiency of evidence for policy makers) but does not provide an interpretation of results in the context of other relevant evidence.

elements.quote:
our review highlights substantial heterogeneity, inconsistencies and perceived errors in the recorded information across source country and regional registries. 

... Inevitably there is a degree of subjectivity in this process leading to possible errors in classification within our database; however, this was minimised by ensuring that all categorical attributes were clearly and prospectively standardised, defined and documented prior to extraction.

... Reliable assessment of the inclusion of vulnerable populations among registered studies was hampered by the limited information included in study registries.

... For this reason, caution should be raised in the interpretation of many initiatives currently presenting the raw WHO ICTRP registry data.
elements.reason: The discussion explicitly describes limitations of the included evidence/registry data (e.g., heterogeneity, inconsistencies, perceived errors, subjectivity in classification, limited information for vulnerable populations) and provides caution about interpreting the raw registry data.

elements.quote: Although two individuals (at least one of whom was a medical doctor) reviewed each included trial record, extraction of manual variables was not blinded.
elements.reason: The Discussion section describes a limitation of the review process (manual variable extraction was not blinded).

elements.quote: For this reason, caution should be raised in the interpretation of many initiatives currently presenting the raw WHO ICTRP registry data.
elements.reason: The Discussion links the limitations of the review/process and underlying registry information to an impact on interpretation (caution when interpreting initiatives based on raw data).

elements.quote: While the mobilisation of the scientific community is admirable, this review illustrates a lack of coordination and duplication of effort that will ultimately delay definitive results of key interventions.
elements.reason: The Discussion describes delays in obtaining results for interventions, but it does not explicitly discuss implications for practice.

elements.quote: The proliferation of such studies will likely result in underpowered studies individually unable to generate meaningful evidence for policy makers.
elements.reason: The Discussion explicitly states an implication for policy makers (i.e., meaningful evidence for policy makers may be limited).
No explicit recommendations for future research are provided in the retrieved evidence.
The retrieved evidence does not report the review register name and registration number, nor does it explicitly state that the review was not registered.
